cards.title: Stage 2, first pieces
cards.text: Primer 0.3 has the first narrated animation, the map, five new answer forms and your 0.2 notes. Mark each part.
cards.why: The voice can only really be judged on your phone: whether it plays, how it sounds, and what it does to music you're playing.
cards.details:
To update: close Primer fully and open it again. Profile shows the version at the bottom; it should say 0.3.0.

The animation is between the two hurricane lessons. Its voice is Heart; Profile, Narrators lets you pick another of your four for each subject. With Voice off it plays from the captions, a tap per line.

Not in yet: review that remembers what you've learned, and the other new parts. Review comes next.

parts.title: The narrated animation
parts.text: "The storm's engine": six lines read aloud while the globe moves on the words, with a moment where you tap the ocean. Tap the picture to pause; the buttons go back or skip a line. Does the voice play, and does your music pause, duck or keep going?

parts.title: Buttons and the chest
parts.text: Buttons sink when pressed and come back, with no jiggle and no shadow under them. The chest is redrawn: dim ahead, glinting when it's next, open once opened.

parts.title: New answer forms
parts.text: Dial (with a redrawn palm), Pile, String, Sort and Snap, as you picked, all checked and revealed the same way. Try them in Practice, Answer forms, at the bottom; that's also where to check for slivers when dragging.

parts.title: One map, globe or flat
parts.text: The globe is now one map part with the projection as a setting: globe, or three flat maps. Every tool works on all of them: names, the four styles, borders, routes that draw themselves, a storm moving along a track. Practice, Map. The flat map starts small; lessons will start it zoomed in.

parts.title: Spacing
parts.text: Steps share the screen better: the question at the top, a picture growing to fill the room, the answer in the middle of what's left. Look at the slider steps in the first lesson.
